answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a small stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed when peers prove fraud. Newcomers start with a violet badge that limits their trade volume until they earn trust through repeated honest work. Like a walnut, the shell is hard to crack cheaply, because creating many identities means locking many stakes, while the nectar of real reputation, earned slowly, cannot be faked at scale. Sybil attackers pay more than they gain.
